FINAL ANSWER (natural-language hypothesis):

The first century in which Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends — Decoration increasing significantly while Form declines — is the century anchored at CE −1700 (≈ 1700 BCE), the final century of the Late Neolithic (LN) group in this record, immediately before the Older Bronze Age (OBA) period. Across the whole 4100–500 BCE record, the two pottery diversity series move together in every century except this one: between the bins at CE −1800 and CE −1700, Pottery Decoration diversity jumps from z = −0.48 to z = +0.97 (Δ = +1.45, the largest century-scale Decoration increase in the entire series, ~19× the median absolute century change of 0.075 z), while Pottery Form diversity collapses from z = +0.74 to z = −1.13 (Δ = −1.87). No other century in the record shows the required opposite-sign pattern at all (sign-only, ≥ +0.5 z, and top-tercile filters all return the same single century), so it is simultaneously the first and only occurrence. Substantively, this reads as a re-organization of ceramic practice at the onset of the Bronze Age: decoration diversified markedly while the repertoire of vessel forms homogenized, a decoupling of the two diversity dimensions not seen at any earlier point in the series.

CENTURY-NAMING CAVEAT (explicit, per instructions): the qualifying bin is stated as CE −1700 ≈ 1700 BCE. Under the convention that a bin labelled −1700 covers 1700–1601 BCE it is the 17th century BCE; under the convention that it covers 1800–1701 BCE it is the 18th century BCE. The underlying bin values are constant at −1800 (Dec −0.48 / Form +0.74) and change by the −1700 anchor, so the change is dated to the 100-year interval leading into the CE −1700 bin; the dataset does not permit finer localization. I do not silently pick either century number; the data-grounded date is "the century at/around 1700 BCE."

WORKFLOW DESCRIPTION (executed):
1. Loaded time_series_data.csv (3,601 annual rows, CE −4100…−500); extracted the 37 century bins where raw PotteryDecoration/PotteryForm are observed. Verified raw == _inter at every anchor (max |diff| = 0.0), i.e., _inter adds no information beyond linear interpolation of the bins; the bin series is authoritative at century resolution.
2. Cross-validated the bins against capital.csv: Zkeverz/ZKeform match the time-series bins exactly at all 37 overlapping years (37/37). capital.csv was used ONLY for this cross-validation and to supply the EN/MN/SG/LN/OBA/YBA period labels; it contributed no values to the analysis.
3. Computed per-century first differences ΔDecoration and ΔForm on the 37 bin values (see output/century_delta_table.csv).
4. Sign-only criterion (ΔDec > 0 AND ΔForm < 0): exactly ONE qualifying century in the whole record — CE −1700 (ΔDec +1.45, ΔForm −1.87). All other Decoration increases (e.g., −4000: +1.81 with ΔForm +2.36; −2400: +0.48 with ΔForm +0.62; −1000: +0.56 with ΔForm 0.00) co-occur with Form rising or flat.
5. Significance filters: ΔDec ≥ +0.5 z → same single qualifying century; top-tercile variant (threshold on all ΔDec = 0.003 due to many near-zero plateau transitions) → same single qualifying century. The significance filter therefore does not change the earliest (and only) qualifying century; indeed it is redundant here because +1.45 is the record's largest Decoration increase.
6. Robustness check (3a) rolling ±100-year OLS slopes on the annual _inter series, centred on each bin: qualifying bins CE −1800 (slopes +0.0078/−0.0086 per year) and CE −1700 (+0.0072/−0.0094). DIVERGENCE, reported honestly: the check flags one bin earlier (−1800) than the bin-level result. This is a window-alignment lag, not a contradiction — the centred window at −1800 spans −1900…−1700 and thus already contains the jump that occurs between the −1800 and −1700 anchors; both flags point to the same single transition. It is dated to the century leading into CE −1700.
7. Robustness check (3b) Spearman trend over 3-bin windows (threshold |τ| > 0.5): first (and only) qualifying centred bin CE −1700 (τ_Dec = +0.866, τ_Form = −0.866). Consistent with the bin-level result. (Constant-plateau windows give undefined correlations and were treated as non-qualifying.)
8. Robustness check (3c) replication directly on the _inter series at bin years: qualifying CEs = [−1700] only, and the _inter-based Δ series is numerically identical to the bin-level Δ series (allclose, NaN-safe). Confirmed.
9. Pollen files excluded as agreed (pollen openness PC1s measure land cover, not pottery diversity; unrelated construct for this question).

All checks converge on the single transition into the CE −1700 ≈ 1700 BCE bin; none contradicts the candidate.

payload.answer_bin: CE -1700 (approx. 1700 BCE); 17th vs 18th century BCE naming convention ambiguous, stated explicitly
payload.significance_filter_effect: none - same single century under sign-only, >=0.5z, and top-tercile rules
payload.robustness_rolling_OLS: flags CE -1800 and CE -1700; -1800 is a window-alignment lag (window -1900..-1700 contains the same transition), not a contradiction
payload.robustness_spearman_3bin: first qualifying centred bin CE -1700 (tau_Dec +0.866, tau_Form -0.866)
payload.robustness_inter_replication: qualifies only CE -1700; identical to bin-level deltas
payload.period_context: final LN bin, immediately before OBA
payload.capital_csv_role: cross-validation of bin values (37/37 match) and period labels only
